statement: For a specified pair of K-state CTMC probe kernels with permutation-orbit gap gamma>0, unknown shared full-rank KxK categorical emission matrix E, supplied or certified pi_i>=p_*>0, conditionally iid reads during pure blocks, and a paid positive slow action with calibrated hold-plus-ramp no-change bounds, a finite-horizon confidence-spent doubling test (returning UNKNOWN on failed certification) has error at most alpha and uses O(K/(p_* gamma^2) kappa^-2 polylog) reads over O(K/(p_* gamma^2) log(K/alpha)) founders for covered kappa. This assumes the action/emission interface and does not validate a physical implementation.
novelty_boundary: Concentration, HMM identifiability and likelihood testing are established prior art. The fixed-pair construction is conditional on a paid near-freeze primitive with ramps budgeted; novelty/priority UNKNOWN. The kappa^-4 lower bound is only for the stated independent two-read pair law, not passive multi-time likelihoods. An optimal likelihood on the same active data is at least as informed; no strict advantage is shown.
costs: Fixed design uses m=O(K gamma^-2 log(K/alpha)) transitions per row; Nc=O(p_*^-1 log(K/alpha)) calibration founders; Nt=O((m+log(K/alpha))/p_*) probe founders; B=Nc+2Nt blocks; R_J=O(kappa^-2 log(BJ/alpha)) repeated reads/block. Charge R_j Delta and ramps per block, nominal probe, readout, calibration, founders, culture, exposure, viability/recovery and actuator. Must have q_ramp<alpha/(4B) and positive rho above hardware floor. Conservative witness at kappa=0.1 uses about 3.09e11 frames and assumes q_ramp=0; no physical advantage follows.
falsifier: Emission drift, non-independent/path-integrated reads, unbounded jump/ramp disturbance, zero or uncertified state occupancy, hardware slowdown floor, or gamma=0 invalidates the theorem's applicability.
next_gate: Find a named system with stable repeated emissions, independent native founders or a proved dependence substitute, and a finite protocol-wide one-sided transition bound including ramps at a positive hardware-feasible setting. Then compare active and passive likelihoods at matched walltime and detected-photon dose with all calibration/action costs.

statement: For the explicit three-state stationary cycle pair and E_kappa=kappa I+(1-kappa)11^T/3, the fixed passive two-read pair law has KL O(kappa^4), so fixed-error tests require Omega(kappa^-4) independent pairs even with known nuisance parameters.
novelty_boundary: Existing fixed pair-law baseline; not a universal lower bound for all passive trajectories or controls.
costs: Two reads per independent founder; Omega(kappa^-4) pairs for fixed error in this stated family.
falsifier: Failure of the exact J0-J1 identity or the small-kappa KL expansion for the stated family.
next_gate: Compare only against a clearly matched baseline action set.

statement: For the specified two-world three-daughter CLE alias under direct semantic family labels, B-only fixed sampling is minimax among adaptive allocation policies; nine B founders are the smallest fixed n with minimax error at most 0.05, and every sequential policy with maximum error delta needs expected B count at least kl(1-delta,delta)/(0.5 log 3) in each world.
novelty_boundary: Exact finite-sample specialization for a previously constructed two-world pair; standard likelihood-ratio and data-processing arguments. Not unrestricted CLE discovery.
costs: One independent founder per action-B assay; charge follow-up to first division, delivered dose, barcoding, three daughter reads, and fixed calibration costs.
falsifier: Any unmodeled difference in action A, failure of family record labels, founder dependence, censoring not in the likelihood, or additional candidate mechanisms invalidates the two-world likelihood.
next_gate: Compare the exact test with the prior Hoeffding control using the same specified assay and validate semantic labels/dose delivery.

statement: Selected reversible cryo-arrest protocols support paid repeated imaging in specific living-cell assays but do not establish a uniform scalar fate-state slowdown, stable E, or the near-freeze ramp bound q_ramp+rho Lambda R Delta<alpha/(4B) required by the theorem.
novelty_boundary: The source protocols are application-specific and do not supply the mathematical action assumptions.
costs: Cooling/warming, DMSO and medium changes, frame timing/exposure, calibration, viability and recovery, culture, and failed tracks.
falsifier: Measure a large ramp/hold state-change bound, drifted emissions, bleaching, or unacceptable time/viability.
next_gate: Acquire the target-state transition envelope, repeated-frame emissions, ramp bound and all-in costs.

statement: NV 14N nuclear-spin fluorescence is a source-supported repeated-read testbed; axial field and RIM duty/wait controls measurably alter persistence. Sources do not provide a ramp-inclusive one-sided transition bound, invariant emissions across controls, independent-founder interface for this theorem, or equal-resource likelihood comparison. Applicability remains UNKNOWN.
novelty_boundary: Experiments establish application-specific repeated fluorescence and persistence control, not the model theorem, novelty or an information advantage.
costs: Photon/RIM count, optical electron repolarization, microwave/RF control, magnet ramp/settle and alignment, action-specific calibration, waiting time, detection efficiency and failed tracks; equal-resource likelihood comparison is unpublished.
falsifier: A same-device matched experiment fails to show lower confidence-bounded state disturbance under the action, or emissions/action kernel shifts erase discrimination at matched walltime and photon budget.
next_gate: Acquire raw photon sequences and action schedules; estimate action-specific emissions and a one-sided transition confidence set including ramps, account dependence across reads, and compare exact sequential-instrument likelihoods at matched walltime and detected-photon dose.
